Each record covers path/kind/permission mode/sha256(file bytes or symlink target UTF-8). Deleted tracked entries retain explicit null mode/hash. Existing gitlink entries cover index mode160000, exact gitlinkCommit and SHA256 of UTF8 gitlink:commit; not external checkout bytes.

criteriaVerbatim: 1. Bind the complete current candidate before reading implementation. Required proof: exact committed SHA and a sorted bytes-plus-mode manifest covering the delivered source, configuration, lockfiles, generated dist, experiment executables/manifests and relevant untracked artifacts; provide algorithm, exclusions, file count and digest, and explain untracked/generated inclusion. Exclusions cannot remove shipped behavior or evidence essential to acceptance. Establish the relationship between any uncommitted snapshot and the eventual committed PR. PASS: the same identity is used by both final reviewers and all applicable validation. FIX-FIRST: delivered code/artifacts differ from the reviewed snapshot. BLOCKED: identity, exclusions or correspondence are unavailable. A path, branch name or bare digest is insufficient.

2. Preserve complete approved scope and independent authorship. Required proof: G1–G9 traceability to the signed design digest f473c5dfff23221fabbcb2aec89880e3199f572ba4dd098ab4be8258a82b79f2 and this matrix, plus independent implementation and separate quality reviewers. Phase B findings must distinguish code reads, attributable reused outputs and unresolved hypotheses. PASS: all obligations remain represented and reviews assess the same candidate. FIX-FIRST: silent scope reduction, fabricated completion or author self-certification substitutes for independent review. BLOCKED: governing artifact or review independence cannot be established.

3. Trace producers through consuming dispatch. Required proof: every introduced engine value, typed completion/timeout failure, cancellation signal, final-tool result, workflow option/event, usage record, snapshot and JEV answer crossing a boundary is followed to its actual receiving switch/router/filter/loop and final consumer. PASS: explicit handling or a correct existing catch-all preserves the intended behavior, failure and usage semantics. FIX-FIRST: a patch-introduced value is dropped, misclassified, ignored or silently falls back. BLOCKED: a necessary consuming implementation is unavailable. Export/type declarations alone do not prove integration.

4. Preserve the imported source graph and initial tree. Required proof: Mikro 62894e49314bad07382492ac074ea96df6776f61 is an ancestor, import is the required non-squash two-parent integration, and the initial imported mikro/ tree equals the clean source tree; relate it to Genie base edf9c7024b1a4417b79b6c13f5e9386c92742bf0. PASS: graph and tree receipts agree. FIX-FIRST: squashed/copied import, incorrect source or imported WIP. BLOCKED: original tree/import receipts are unavailable.

5. Preserve original checkouts, unrelated WIP and operator state. Required proof: before/after original Mikro HEAD, index identity, dirty/untracked file inventories and byte hashes, specifically installer/CLI/CHANGELOG WIP; original Genie work and operator settings/auth/key/helper inventories remain unchanged except explicitly assigned additions. Receipts must be secret-safe. PASS: exact preservation is demonstrated. FIX-FIRST: unauthorized changes, deletion or git-state movement. BLOCKED: preservation cannot be established from attributable before/after evidence. Production brain runtime, main and production installation are outside mutation scope.

6. Maintain independent package discovery, ownership and release boundaries. Required proof: Mikro remains npm/package-lock with Node >=22.19.0 and independent Node ambient types; Genie remains Bun/bun.lock. Root discovery exclusions cover only the independently gated subtree and preserve the original root test set. Review legacy-catalog collection/retirement authority and nested standalone-update guard through consuming paths; the guard rejects before owner/journal/fetch/reset/clean mutation while legitimate standalone behavior remains supported. PASS: subtree history/skills are outside Genie retirement authority, both package contracts work, and Genie runtime has no Mikro dependency or payload addition. FIX-FIRST: exclusion hides root regressions, authority crosses into imported content, nested updates mutate it, or release bundling changes. BLOCKED: boundary inventory or owning behavior proof is missing.

7. Use the exact compatible SDK family. Required proof: package manifest, lock resolution and actual compiled imports of coding-agent, pi-ai and directly imported agent-core are 1.0.2, with no incompatible duplicate provider identity; actual package-local callsites are migrated. Built-in deepseek/deepseek-flash resolves from the pinned catalog. PASS: dependency and execution identities agree. FIX-FIRST: incorrect pin, stale APIs or incompatible resolved family. BLOCKED: installed resolution/compiled identity is not attributable.

8. Preserve provider configuration and truthful stop semantics. Required proof: success responses and configured custom-provider auth, sampling/cache/output controls remain effective; actual error, aborted and length scenarios yield LLMCompletionError with the correct stopReason, secret-safe message and reported usage. Trace usage through SDK/runtime/footer consumers. PASS: failures cannot become empty success or valid structured answers, and reported usage is retained once. FIX-FIRST: false success, lost/doubled usage, credential disclosure or provider behavior regression. BLOCKED: actual provider-failure boundary evidence is missing.

9. Bound ordinary transport retries without hidden replacement behavior. Required proof: owning tests and actual boundary evidence for default maxRetries=3, explicit zero, caller propagation and termination; preserve attempts and available usage rather than concealing retry costs. PASS: configured controls govern execution and no new unapproved retry layer appears. FIX-FIRST: zero is replaced by the default, retries escape bounds or callers ignore the option. BLOCKED: effective attempts/options cannot be established.

10. Handle FINAL values safely and honestly. Required proof: actual compiled RLM/parser behavior for bare safe identifiers, quoted literals, missing variables, ellipsis and arbitrary expressions. PASS: safe identifiers resolve existing variables, quoted values remain literal, arbitrary expressions are not evaluated, and missing/ellipsis values receive repair feedback rather than successful finalization. FIX-FIRST: unsafe evaluation or a false final answer. BLOCKED: parser-to-runtime behavior lacks attributable proof.

11. Recover timeouts without replay or stale-child corruption. Required proof: real Python/bridge timeout with an observable side effect executed exactly once; typed REPLTimeoutError; terminate/wait/detach old child, reject stale bridge replies, restore only saved initial context/tools, visibly report lost user variables, and exercise subsequent allowed-turn behavior. Failed restart and exhausted deadline must terminate. PASS: a fresh live namespace continues only when allowed, without replay. FIX-FIRST: duplicated side effects, retained dead/stale namespace, silent state loss or restart outside limits. BLOCKED: actual subprocess/bridge evidence is unavailable.

12. Finalize inside every declared budget. Required proof: actual call-count receipts and owning behavior tests for last-turn schema finalization, failed validation, maxIterations, token/cost caps and deadline; trace LLMCompletionError usage once. PASS: final turn is included in the cap and returns only a schema-valid final or truthful terminal failure, with no extra forced-final completion. FIX-FIRST: an additional model turn, overspent budget, discarded failure usage or invalid answer marked successful. BLOCKED: measured calls/limits are absent.

13. Enforce explicit engine precedence and clean cutover. Required proof: compiled MCP and SDK behavior for rlm|pi|prime|prime-sdk; omitted engine uses RLM, explicit call overrides agent then default, including generic query; obsolete backend keys and unknown/empty/non-string values fail before billing. Trace all repository callers and effective-engine compatibility when discovery degrades. PASS: no shape heuristic, alias or silent fallback remains. FIX-FIRST: precedence/rejection differs, a stale caller bypasses the selector or a value silently routes incorrectly. BLOCKED: active-caller inventory or compiled selector proof is missing. Prime support remains compatible but is neither re-pinned nor scored.

Required proof: real SDK session using isolated ModelRuntime/SettingsManager/SessionManager/ResourceLoader and only scoped read/grep/glob/git/emit_done; adversarial out-of-root, symlink, mutation, ambient resource/instruction/plugin and git-configuration probes. Git operations disable external diff/textconv/fsmonitor/pager/hooks and config-environment injection; containment follows realpaths. PASS: these boundaries hold through actual tool dispatch. FIX-FIRST: any escape, ambient credential/resource loading or mutation-capable path. BLOCKED: dependency-backed adversarial execution evidence is missing.

Required proof: real tool loop exercising a valid final, missing/invalid final, final schema precedence and both validations, repeated finals, stop-after-turn, usage/limits/progress, cancellation/deadline and disposal. PASS: first accepted final wins; no copied-last-paragraph/REPL fallback; terminal errors and actual usage remain truthful; cleanup completes. FIX-FIRST: invalid/missing answer succeeds, later final overwrites accepted data, execution ignores limits or resources survive cancellation. BLOCKED: actual loop/lifecycle evidence is missing.

16. Preserve outward MCP and SDK contracts. Required proof: compiled MCP and Genie caller execution through both engines, including failure paths, structuredContent {answer, session_id}, priced footer, history, progress heartbeat and classification. Optional cancellation, if added, reaches every affected backend without obsolete aliases. PASS: all existing consumers accept the unchanged envelope and accounting exactly once. FIX-FIRST: dropped result/session/progress/failure data or incorrect pricing/history. BLOCKED: consumer-boundary evidence is unavailable.

18. Separate proposal authorization from citation evidence. PASS: NEW authorizes a proposal only, never fabricates existing-file/citation evidence. FIX-FIRST: declaration leakage validates an ordinary citation or escapes repository authority. BLOCKED: consuming verifier proof is missing.

19. Produce honest parent-tree fixtures and separate scores. Required proof: actual fixture-generator CLI output binds source/evaluation/parent commits, repository/tree hashes and added-file provenance; runtime sees the parent tree with implementation absent. Score NEW, files and citations independently, and exercise failure answers after success. PASS: no answer leakage or stale-success inheritance. FIX-FIRST: added implementation remains available, provenance is wrong, or failure retains previous successful scores. BLOCKED: parent identities or actual generation/evaluation evidence are missing.

20. Cut over repository defaults without changing operator configuration. Required proof: all active repository agent defaults and root .mikro/mikro.yaml use built-in deepseek/deepseek-flash; obsolete root deepseek-api and Pro configuration are removed while immutable historical baseline artifacts and operator-owned auth/settings remain untouched. A compiled generic mikro_query using repository configuration without a model override must actually resolve and call Flash. PASS: owning behavioral regressions and real query agree. FIX-FIRST: stale/shadowing provider config, prohibited calls or operator-state mutation. BLOCKED: no-model-override execution/provenance is missing.

21. Provision distinct keys explicitly and additively. Required proof: explicit origin/project/credential references; actual supported CPA additive/idempotent operation; distinct assigned Genie/brain project keys; private directory 0700 and files 0600; unrelated keys and operator state preserved. Endpoints remain disabled until configured and credentials do not appear in argv/logs/source/manifests/commits/chat. PASS: project isolation and permissions are demonstrated. FIX-FIRST: shared/wrong key, destructive provision, unsafe permissions or secret disclosure. BLOCKED: sanctioned provisioning/authentication or safe preservation evidence is unavailable.

22. Authenticate catalog and inference with invocation-scoped project credentials. Required proof: actual project-key catalog and real calls for assigned projects, advertised model IDs/provenance retained, and concurrent/sequential SDK callers cannot inherit another project's credentials through global mutation. PASS: only authorized advertised identities are used, no invented aliases or Pro/Claude calls. FIX-FIRST: wrong attribution, ambient/global credential leakage or fabricated catalog identities. BLOCKED: actual catalog/call/credential-scope proof is missing.

23. Capture only authorized, source-linked aggregates. Required proof: actual manual juice usage/analyze, project-key viewer login, in-memory cookie and /key-overview, /key-analysis and /key-analysis/latency; attributable version/session/logout evidence; sanitized snapshots preserve URL/query/project/key epoch/returned range/timezone/fetch time/hash. PASS: responses are project-scoped, capabilities distinguish aggregate access from unavailable request/payload export, unknown cost/time remains unknown, and aggregate spend is not canonical runtime billing. FIX-FIRST: admin escalation, request/conversation export, invented IDs/zero costs, secret disclosure or duplicate billing. BLOCKED: authorized viewer session or actual snapshots are unavailable.

Required proof: configured full endpoint/model/key reference and actual CLI-to-extractWithJev wiring; official {state,model,questions} payload, bounded sanitized source-linked candidate IDs, cancellation, Choice with abstention, and optional Noul/Score only within the same requested call. PASS: answers and usage are observed, source reattachment is local and exact, invalid transport/schema is an explicit error. FIX-FIRST: fabricated/empty successful extraction, unmapped selections or lost source/usage. BLOCKED: real response or sanctioned access cannot be obtained. The scope's expired AWS SSO description is not itself current proof of an unreachable endpoint; require exact attempted sanctioned discovery/auth sources and current failure evidence, with no silent public-cloud substitution.

26. Keep ordinary runs free of instrumentation inference. Required proof: trace ordinary model, MCP and workflow paths and attributable call/event observations; extraction is reachable only by the explicit configured manual action. PASS: ordinary runs perform no JEV/Keeper extraction or extra instrumentation model call. FIX-FIRST: automatic extraction/inference/retries or source mutation. BLOCKED: call-boundary evidence is missing.

27. Prove every named actual runtime surface. Required proof: original bounded provider/REPL/final/citation failures reproduced at their actual boundaries, then attributable repaired compiled execution through MCP and Genie; real Python/bridge, Pi SDK/tools, generic query, fixture CLI, configured Juice/JEV and installed CLI/MCP surfaces as required above. PASS: no source-only substitute, permanent scaffold, fake fallback or stale dist. FIX-FIRST: demonstrated failure or reachable omitted surface. BLOCKED: an exact external prerequisite prevents the required real execution. Unit mocks and source-text assertions cannot replace these proofs.

28. Freeze fixture, arm and runtime identities before outcomes. Required proof: four Genie/brain existing/new-directory fixtures match the original FROZEN-FIXTURES.json bytes; pre-outcome manifests identify every Flash arm, separately available curated candidate IDs and catalog exclusions, source/parent trees, launcher/runtime/artifact/schema/prompt/pricing hashes, repetitions and concurrency=1. FIX-FIRST: post-outcome cohort selection, changed fixture bytes, answer leakage, unapproved models or scored Prime. BLOCKED: original freeze identity/timing or arm definitions are missing. 29. Complete all required fixture runs without survivor filtering. Required proof: all 36 Flash runs across the frozen four-fixture/three-arm/three-repetition matrix, and every separately frozen available curated candidate cell with three repetitions on matched upgraded RLM/Pi conditions. Preserve every attempt, failure, retry and unknown; explain unavailable candidates from the pre-outcome catalog, not unfavorable outcomes. PASS: complete immutable run records match the freeze. FIX-FIRST: missing reachable cells, substitutions, discarded failures or fabricated results. BLOCKED: exact required service access/records are unavailable. Availability exclusions cannot silently shrink the fixed Flash obligation.

30. Report measured outcomes and honest selection statistics. Required proof: per-cell verified success and file/NEW/citation metrics, run and all-attempt latency p50/p90, cost per verified success, cost coverage, cap share and repetition dispersion; methods and attempt denominators are explicit, and unknown usage is never zero. Selection requires verified-success parity in each repository/model cell and no real-workflow SHIP/repair regression. PASS: claims are supported at the measured scope; ties/insufficient evidence remain inconclusive. FIX-FIRST: speed-only recommendation, pooled success hiding a failing cell, unpriced cost claim or omitted attempts. BLOCKED: required outcome/accounting inputs are unavailable. No automatic routing or promotion follows from a recommendation.

31. Prove actual native workflow identity before scoring. Required proof: unscored actual DSH-loader/non-Claude-route smoke and experiment-local observer, then each scored run binds real workflow UUID, seq, childId, native persisted own-suffix assistant/message and assistant/attempt usage, tool/call events and lifecycle timestamps. Use the actual saved wish.js, not a surrogate. PASS: observed identities join to durable native records and only own-run events are counted. FIX-FIRST: synthetic IDs, DSH success journals alone, wrong sessions, inherited/forked double counting or consumer redesign. BLOCKED: native persistence/identity/observer evidence is inaccessible.

32. Complete the 18 genuine wish variants with isolation. Required proof: two bounded objectives × offload-rlm/offload-pi/offload-off × three repetitions, each using independent repository/common-directory/state roots; actual native models obey the no-Pro/no-Claude rule, outcomes/SHIP/repair counts and both offload treatments are observed. PASS: all genuine runs, failures and treatment identities are retained. FIX-FIRST: surrogate pipeline, reused contaminated state, decorative treatment, missing reachable runs or forbidden calls. BLOCKED: exact native launcher/model access or actual run receipts are unavailable.

33. Establish full accounting before completing workflow comparison or appending reports. Required proof: measured native stage tokens/tools/durations and priced offloads, explicit ownership of assistant/attempt/message/tool events, parent/fork exclusion, and compatibility with unchanged capture/export/wish-report consumers. Required top-level fields must be completely measured; missing fields remain unknown, not synthetic workflow IDs or token zeros. Keeper aggregate spend is contextual, never an extra canonical charge. PASS: fully measured compatible records only are appended, each once, and all required comparison accounting is complete. FIX-FIRST: fabricated/partial append, duplicate billing, existing-consumer redesign or implementation-caused accounting loss. BLOCKED: exact unavailable native accounting prevents completion even when all 18 runs have genuine outcomes. Preserved partial receipts are useful evidence but do not satisfy this criterion.

34. Keep delivered code, documentation and generated artifacts coherent. Required proof: affected schema/provider/runtime/CLI/monorepo docs and changelogs match the implemented contract; generated dist is built from the pinned source, obsolete selectors/callers/shims and throwaway smokes are removed while durable proofs and required experiment execution remain. PASS: no scaffold, fake fallback or obsolete active path remains. FIX-FIRST: shipped/runtime mismatch, misleading behavior documentation or unfinished implementation. Nonblocking prose/style nits do not invalidate correctness. BLOCKED: artifact/source correspondence is unavailable.

35. Preserve both complete aggregate gates and actual install/release proof. Required attributable coordinator outputs: npm --prefix mikro run deps:ci, build, check and test; isolated standalone scripts/smoke-install-update.sh; bun install --frozen-lockfile and the complete bun run check under the existing host lock. Include command/cwd/environment corrections, exit status, pass/fail/skip totals and artifact identity. Retain existing release verification, actual CLI/MCP smokes and original Genie binary/tarball payload contract; Mikro CI independently covers npm lock/build/tests/install contract. PASS: every required gate and actual artifact surface passes at the candidate. FIX-FIRST: genuine failed gate, narrowed replacement, source suppression or changed Genie release payload. BLOCKED: missing/stale/non-attributable full gate or artifact proof. Only documented inherited NO_COLOR/TMPDIR corrections are acceptable; reviewer executes nothing in this assignment.

36. Obtain independent, current reviews after bounded repairs. Required proof: final implementation review and separate security/maintainability/performance quality review cover the complete scope at the same identity; dispositions of reproduced blockers and repair budgets B=2 plus quality cap=1 are retained. Relevant repairs invalidate prior reviews/gates and require current attributable reassessment. PASS: independent source/feature reviews have no blocking gaps and limitations are explicit. FIX-FIRST: unresolved reproduced blockers or relevant repair not reassessed. BLOCKED: independent current review/evidence is missing. Prior SHIP language is evidence to inspect, not a substitute for this review.

37. Deliver a current, merge-ready dev PR without promotion. Required proof: exact committed scope, pushed head, PR targeting Genie dev, current live base ref, head SHA and three-dot file scope, merge-cleanliness against that live base, and required remote CI checks attached to the current head. Review current inbound threads/dispositions without inferring resolution from comments. Reconcile local manifest/compiled artifacts/gates/reviews with the remote candidate; refresh identity after validation and invalidate evidence when relevant bytes/head change. PASS: current remote and local identities agree, required CI is green, no merge/main promotion/production install occurred, and wish remains IN_PROGRESS pending authorized merge/QA. FIX-FIRST: wrong target, extra/unreviewed files, stale head greens presented as current, conflict, unauthorized promotion or false SHIPPED status. BLOCKED: absent PR, inaccessible/currently incomplete required CI or missing current base/head readback. Neither a PR number nor a worker notification proves delivery.

38. Record exact unreachable prerequisites without waiving obligations. For every unexercised required behavior, identify the criterion, exact missing endpoint/permission/native event or field/environment artifact, sanctioned discovery/access paths attempted, attributable current failure, why remaining reachable work cannot supply the proof, and which claim remains unverified. Complete all reachable adapter/source work and preserve real partial receipts. G9 permits truthful exercised-proof-or-exact-unreachable-prerequisite reporting; it does not convert an unreachable prerequisite into a successful runtime proof, measured accounting, completed comparison or whole-wish SHIP. A precise blocker can satisfy G9's disclosure clause while G8 criterion 33 remains BLOCKED. A vague environment claim, an old expired-token statement or an untried reachable source is insufficient.

39. Issue separate source, comparison and whole-delivery dispositions. Source/feature SHIP requires candidate-bound implementation, consumer compatibility, preservation, required compiled/installed behavioral proof, complete applicable gates and independent review to pass. If these pass but criteria 29–33 remain unresolved solely because full experiment/accounting evidence is unavailable, only 'conditional source SHIP — comparison and whole delivery BLOCKED on [exact criterion/prerequisite]' is permissible; it cannot authorize a whole-scope SHIP/green publication claim. If a required source-feature integration such as actual JEV execution is itself unproved, limit any favorable assessment to inspected source and explicitly mark full feature validation BLOCKED. Comparison SHIP requires complete matched runs, real identities, full accounting and honest statistics; inability to prove performance superiority is an inconclusive result, not permission to lower verified-success parity. Whole-delivery SHIP requires all G1–G9 obligations and current dev-PR remote evidence to pass. A draft/source-reviewable PR, if present, is not the specified whole-delivery merge-ready result.

40. Apply final aggregate triggers without hiding mixed results. SHIP: every applicable criterion for the named verdict scope passes, with no blocking defect or required missing proof. FIX-FIRST: a confirmed implementation, compatibility, isolation, preservation, accounting or delivery violation; a failed required gate; fabricated evidence; or a knowingly omitted reachable obligation. BLOCKED: exact prerequisites/evidence are unavailable so a valid complete assessment cannot be made, including unresolved full accounting. When both kinds occur, lead with FIX-FIRST for confirmed repairable defects and separately enumerate external blockers; never use BLOCKED to erase known bugs. An exact unreachable-prerequisite record is an honest incomplete outcome, not completion. Any later identity change invalidates the affected verdict until re-pinned and reassessed.
